name: Battle radio man, USA, Normandy 1944 (our own design)
about: Made by Tools/battle_units/soldier_usa_radio.py on soldier_usa.py and soldier.py. Metres; x forward, y right, z up. Paints: 0 tunic, 1 trousers, 2 boots, 3 lower, 4 straps, 5 helmet, 6 pack, 7 skin, 8 wood, 9 steel, 10 coat, 11 coat_dark, 12 leather, 13 blanket, 14 hoof, 19 radio (the eyes are painted as boots). near = LOD0, mid = LOD1, far = LOD2, all in the rest pose (arms 45 degrees down). Each point rides on bone `part` and, by `w2` (0 to 0.5), on bone `part2`. Skinning: a bone's turn G = G_parent * q (q from the clip, identity at rest; G of a bone with no track is its parent's), its head X = X_parent + G_parent * (head - head_parent + move), and a point p on it goes to X + G * (p - head). Quaternions are [t, w, x, y, z] in these axes (as Unreal's FQuat). Clips are in place: `stride` is the metres one loop covers; the game moves the unit. A mesh may carry `shade` per point (0 to 1, the wear and seam darkening): its colour is the paint's colour times shade; with no `shade` every point is 1. He is the company's radio man: soldier_usa.py's rifleman (dress, helmet, canteen, first-aid pouch) with the M1 carbine on the weapon bone (0.904 m; semi-automatic: his fire_stand, fire_kneel and fire_prone are soldier_usa.py's, one shot a second, cue rifle_shot), a pistol belt with a pocket of two carbine magazines, and on his back in the haversack's place the SCR-300 set over its battery case (paint 19, radio) with its long whip antenna (3.25 m, up from the set's top left, leaning a little back and out to his left; on its own four bones, below). The handset rides the bolt bone: clipped high on his left suspender strap in every clip, in his left hand and at his left ear in radio_call. His own: radio_call (8 s loop, kneeling, his carbine laid by his left knee): the handset taken off the strap (0.85 s) and put to his ear, radio_squelch at 1.5 s (cue radio_squelch, on the head); he calls, radio_talk at 1.95 s (cue radio_talk, on the head), turns his head to the target and points to it with his right hand; call_support at 5.3 s (no socket, no cue): the call goes through and the battle decides what comes, artillery or an airstrike; he hears the answer and nods, and hangs the handset back on the strap (7.25 s). For an airstrike (in 1944 the target was marked with coloured smoke) the game can mark it with his throw_grenade clip (its grenade_release event) as a coloured smoke grenade. lmg_burst (prone on the aim) fires nothing. The whip is a chain of four bones for the deaths to bend: whip_1 (a child of chest, its head at the antenna's mount on top of the set) to whip_4, laid end to end up the whip to its tip (whip_1 0.86 m, through the base to the second ferrule; the others 0.8125 m each), after the 32 bones (bones 32 to 35, here and in the glb's skin). Near, each section of the whip rides its bone and the ferrules at the joints take the two bones half and half; mid and far, the whip is one straight tube from its foot (whip_1) to its tip (whip_4). In every clip the chain is straight, at rest, but for a gentle sway in walk, run and advance (a few degrees at each joint). GORE TWIN (Tools/battle_units/gore.py): this man with his limbs able to come off at eight joints; see `gore`. Same bones, same sockets first, same faces, helmets and inks as his own file; `clips` is empty for the deaths thread's gore deaths. The helmet triangles (helmet_tris) are no longer the last of each list: the caps follow them, so leave out [first, first + count) only.

helmets.name: plain olive drab
helmets.about: Issue M1 in rough olive drab (cork or sawdust in the paint to kill the shine), the rim and chin-strap loops rubbed toward the steel. No badge as issued.

helmets.name: net
helmets.about: A helmet net over the plain helmet (American fine-mesh nets, or the wider British-made ones issued in England before the landings), worn bare.

helmets.name: net and burlap scrim
helmets.about: The 1944 Normandy look: the wide British-made net with strips of burlap and hessian, green and brown, pushed through it and hanging past the rim.

helmets.name: net and hedgerow leaves
helmets.about: Net with sprigs from the hedgerows of the bocage stuck through it (Normandy, June to August 1944).

helmets.name: net and jungle leaves
helmets.about: Net with broad leaves through it, in the Pacific and Burma.

helmets.name: sergeant's bar
helmets.about: A white bar painted across the back, the mark of a sergeant (officers wore it upright), as many units painted them in Europe from 1944.

helmets.name: road dust
helmets.about: The plain helmet under the white dust of the Normandy lanes in the summer breakout.

helmets.name: mud
helmets.about: Mud smeared on by hand (the autumn and winter of 1944 in Lorraine and the Hurtgen).

helmets.name: whitewash
helmets.about: Whitewash or white paint brushed over in the Ardennes snow (December 1944 to February 1945), rubbed back to the drab at the rim.

helmets.name: white cloth
helmets.about: A piece of bedsheet or mattress cover tied over the helmet in the Ardennes.

about_variety: Variety (Tools/battle_units/variety.py and helmet_finishes.py): one man made into many. `faces` (8): face 0 is the man as he is; for face k, add `move` (metres, this file's axes) to the points listed in `at`, at each level of detail, then colour: every skin-painted point's colour times `tone`, and each point in `tint_at` times its `tint` (the hair, brows, stubble or moustache), all on top of the paint (and `shade`) as usual. `helmets`: his helmet (or cap, ushanka or hood) in the finishes it was worn in. Each is a rigid mesh at near/mid/far in the same form as the file's own meshes (points, facings, paints, triangles, part, part2, w2, and shade where the file has it), with `ink` at each point: -1 paints the point by its paint number as ever; any other value is an index into `inks` (colours, RRGGBB), the colour to paint it instead. To draw a man in a finish, leave out his own helmet's triangles, `helmet_tris[lod]` = [first, count] (they are the last of the list), and draw the finish's mesh skinned on the same bones. Each finish has `season` (any, summer, winter), `front` (any, east, west, south, desert, pacific, china) and `share` (how common it was), and no `from` or `to` month (Brian's standing rule, 26 November 2026: a man's markings and paint never hang on the year). Picking, for each man: the finishes whose season and front fit (any fits all), whatever the battle's date, one chosen by share, and face = a hash of (block id, k) mod 8 and the helmet from another hash of the same, so a man keeps both all battle. When no finish fits his season and front, he wears his own helmet in his army's helmet colour. No swastika, rising-sun flag or fascist badge is drawn: the German eagle decal is left off (its side stays plain paint).

gore.about: Eight cuts at the ragdoll's own joints: upperarm_l/_r (the arm at the shoulder), lowerarm_l/_r (the elbow), thigh_l/_r (the whole leg at the hip), calf_l/_r (the knee). No skin is shared across a cut: at each joint every point rides 100% one side (w2 0 across the cut) and the seam is doubled, so moving a cut bone away from its parent (a bone move in a clip; the battle keeps moves on every bone) takes the limb off clean, with nothing stretched. Each open side is closed by a cap recessed into its own side: torn cloth (the uniform's own paint), a soaked edge (paint `blood`), raw flesh (`wound`) and a short rough bone end (`bone`); at rest the caps are inside him. JOINED: hard weights open the bent joints (the shoulder and hip most: a crack of 5 to 10 cm in a kneel, the caps red inside it). `joined` puts that right: per level of detail a list of points (`points`) with the man's own weights (`part`, `part2`, `w2`) and `cuts`, a mask (bit k for cut k in the order of `cuts` below: 1 upperarm_l, 2 lowerarm_l, 4 upperarm_r, 8 lowerarm_r, 16 thigh_l, 32 calf_l, 64 thigh_r, 128 calf_r). Skin each listed point with the listed weights while none of the cuts in its mask is off, with its own once one is: whole, the twin then moves exactly as his own file (every original point; the seam copies with it) and the caps ride the joint inside him; a cut off takes its own points to hard weights and leaves every other joint whole. (Without it the twin still works, cracked.) Per cut: `bone`, `parent`, `joint` (the cut bone's rest head, these axes), `limb` (the bones that go with it), `sockets` (`wound_<bone>` on the stump, on the parent bone, at the cut's centre facing out of the stump: blood spurts, smoke, the flies; `end_<bone>` on the limb, facing out of its end), and per level of detail `loops` (seam vertices) and for `stump` and `limb` the [first, count] of their cap's points and triangles. Arrays: near, mid and far keep the delivered man's points and triangles first, in order, with their values (only part/part2/w2 changed, at the joints' bands), then the seam copies, then the caps cut by cut. Paints: wound 35, bone 36, blood 37 (`colours`, `new_paints`): darken or colour them as the battle likes. With gore off, draw X.json as ever; with gore on, swap to this file at the hit and play a gore death from its `clips` (the deaths thread's).

about_gore: Gore deaths (Tools/battle_units/falls.py, GORE; Brian, 22 November 2026: "graphic animations if a guy gets shot or blown up", "with limbs coming off"; the art director's notes of 23 November): physics falls as the man's own deaths are, in which a limb is taken off at its joint (the cuts this file's mesh is split at: shoulder, elbow, hip, knee) and flung away from the blast: a low arc, 1 to 3 m high, tumbling 1 to 2 turns a second, 2 to 8 m from a shell (an arm 1 to 4 m, a lower leg 1 to 3 m), lying flat where it lands. From the cut the limb's bone carries a move track: it flies and lands as a body of its own, and lies where it fell for the rest of the battle as he does. Pick, gore on: deaths_gore[stance][kind] by where the burst was against his facing: back (in front of him: thrown back), forward (behind him), side (at his side), under (on his feet or a knee, the burst within a metre, under him: a lower leg off); thrown (die_blast_*: a field gun's or a howitzer's shell: lifted 0.5 to 1.5 m, thrown 2 to 4 m, sliding where he lands); one of the list by a hash of (block id, man). Every stance has a fall from each side (lying: an arm off as he is rolled half away, a lower leg off from behind; on a knee: an arm off from either side) besides the thrown. Each clip's blast_from (and gore_from, clip to side) says where its burst was: front, behind, left, right, under; a side or thrown pick can match left or right by it, and each limb comes to rest 0.5 m or more farther from the burst than it was cut. Events: limb_off at the cut (socket: the wound on the body, wound_<bone>; end: the limb's cut end, end_<bone>, for the blood), limb_fall where the severed limb comes down (x, y, z in his own axes, metres); rifle_off where the rifle leaves his hand and rifle_fall where it first comes down (x, y, z), thrown clear; in some, helmet_off (its middle x y z, v and spin as it leaves his head) and helmet_fall (where it lands; rest, where it stops; upside_down), marks for the effects thread's hook (the helmet's triangles, helmet_tris, ride the head till helmet_off); and knee_down, body_fall, rifle_drop as in every death. Gore off: none of this is loaded.
about_wear: Wear and weather (Tools/battle_units/shade.py; Brian, 22 November 2026: uniforms dirtier the longer a unit is at the front, fresh replacements clean; rain darkens the cloth and splashes the mud higher; snow white on the shoulders and helmets). Per point, at near, mid and far and on each helmet finish's own mesh: `shade` (0.4 to 1) and `tint` (3 a point: red, green, blue) are the look as baked, a man some weeks in the line (wear W 0.6) in dry weather, for drawing paint x shade x tint as ever. `shade_clean`: the same shadow with no dirt (folds, under the straps, pack, belt and helmet brim, worn edges, the cloth's uneven fade). `dirt` (0 to 1): where dust and mud collect in dry weather (boots, leggings and trousers to a little over the knee in splashes, the knees, the seat, elbows, cuffs and hands, a little in the face's creases); `dirt_wet`: the same in rain (mud splashed up the thighs, caked boots, heavier knees and seat, the forearms and the front of the belly from going down in it). `wet` (0 to 1): how much the surface darkens when soaked (wool 1, webbing 0.8, leather 0.6, wood 0.45, helmet paint 0.3, steel 0.2, skin 0.15; less under the pack and the arms). `snow` (0 to 1): how much snow settles there on a man standing (open to the sky and facing up: the helmet's crown, shoulders, pack, the tops of the arms and boots; little on skin and steel). MIXING, per man: W = wear, from how long his unit has been at the front (0.1 a fresh replacement or a new unit, 1 six weeks or more in the line; replacements in a veteran unit stay low until they have been in it a while), R = rain (0 dry ground to 1 soaked) and S = snow (0 to 1), both from the battle's weather draw. In sRGB 0 to 1: base = paint x shade_clean x (1 - 0.35 x wet x R) (x the face's tone and tint); d = (dirt + (dirt_wet - dirt) x R) x W; soil = (DUST + (MUD - DUST) x R) x shade_clean, DUST (0.60, 0.54, 0.43) dry dust and dried mud, MUD (0.27, 0.21, 0.15) wet mud (or the field's own soil, lighter dry); colour = base + (soil - base) x 0.85 x d; then toward snow (0.92, 0.94, 0.97) x (0.6 + 0.4 x shade_clean) by 0.9 x snow x S. The gore paints (wound, bone, blood): shade 1, no dirt, wet or snow. Mid and far carry the near's, their shade eased off (90 % and 75 % of the darkening).
about_pack: pack_tris (pack_range.py): his pack and all his webbing (belt, straps, pouches, bags, canteen, shovel, bayonet, gas-mask can, rolls, a radio or aid bags), one run of triangles at each level [first, count], as helmet_tris: leave it out for a man with no pack (a downed pilot, a crew out of a tank) and draw nothing in its place, the cloth is whole under it. Buttons, badges, the helmet's chin strap and the weapon are not in it.
